english.title: Racially aggravated criminal damage
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse,

(A)_[destroyed **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damaged **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_

(C)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY VALUE..)]_
(D)_[to a value unknown]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged which was racially aggravated in accordance with section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971 and section 30(1) and (2) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is OBSOLETE. Now see CJS Code CD98074 and Offence Wording H10011.

(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) Section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 shall have effect as if the person to whom the property belongs or is treated as belonging for the purposes of the Criminal Damage Act 1971 were the victim of the offence.
(iii) For the religiously or religiously/racially wordings see offence wordings H4728 and H4729.
(iv) If this offence is tried by a Crown Court, it is open to the jury to return a lesser charge of simple criminal damage. In R v Fennell (2000) the point was raised that if the damage was under £5000 the offence is treated as summary and the Crown Court have no jurisdiction. However, F was unsuccessful, the offence is still either way and the Crown Court can deal with such a matter.
